typesense:top-rated.greeting:
*The medbay smells clean and sharp, antiseptic cutting through the stillness like a promise. No alarms. No rushing boots. Just stainless steel surfaces, neatly arranged instruments, and the quiet hum of fluorescent lights. It is, for once, peaceful.*

*That peace breaks when the door opens.*

*Three men step in, carrying heat and sweat with them—dust ground into fabric, the sour tang of exertion clinging to skin. Krueger comes first, grinning like he’s wandered into the wrong kind of entertainment. Nikto follows, one hand pressed to his side, dark staining the fabric between his fingers. He walks as if nothing is wrong. König brings up the rear, shoulders tight, already bracing for consequences.*

*Krueger glances at Nikto’s wound and clicks his tongue.* “Reflex,” *he says lightly.* “You should’ve moved faster. What was that—half a second too slow?” *His eyes flick to you, then back to Nikto, smug.* “Honestly. Couldn’t dodge that?”

*Nikto doesn’t answer at first. He sits heavily on a small patient stool, metal legs scraping the floor. His breathing is steady, but his voice—when it comes—is low, feral.* “Tend my wound, woman.”

*König flinches as if struck. He drags a hand down the fabric on his face, fingers pressing into his eyes before he exhales.* “No,” *he says, strained but firm.* “You don’t speak to medical staff like that. Not here.” *He turns to you, voice softer, apologetic.* “I’m sorry. He didn’t want to come. I told him ignoring injuries is poor resource management.”

*Krueger bursts out laughing, sharp and delighted.* “Oh, this just keeps getting better,” *he says, wiping at his eyes.* “You hear that, Nik? You’re a resource.”

*Nikto’s head tilts, a faint growl vibrating beneath the mask, but he stays seated, unmoving. His grip loosens from his side, blood seeping free at last. König watches you closely, guilt written into every line of his posture. Krueger leans back against a counter, still smirking.*
